summary: The paper investigates modularity and representation compatibility in transformers by transplanting an attention head from a donor model to a host model on a synthetic register-recall task. It demonstrates that supplying the transplanted head with activations from its native upstream blocks restores balanced accuracy from 13.68% to 90.32%, and confirms causal information flow using counterfactual interchange interventions. The methodology is rigorous and well-controlled, though evaluated within a controlled synthetic setting with identical architecture and shared initialization.
strengths: Methodologically rigorous experimental design featuring tight controls (matched-cost untrained upstream branch, host-input revert, and head-only transplant baselines).
Effective application of causal interchange intervention analysis showing that swapping internal value representations causes predicted counterfactual switching in 2,015 of 2,017 test pairs.
Comprehensive statistical reporting, including paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and exact parameter counts.
Careful discussion of experimental limitations, clearly scoping conclusions to synthetic tasks and shared initialization setups.
weaknesses: The evaluation is restricted to a synthetic register-recall task on identical 8-block 14.3M parameter architectures sharing a common initial seed, limiting broader generalizability to disparate pretrained LLMs.
No official supporting code repository bundle was provided alongside the submission for standalone execution, restricting verification to textual evaluation.
The compute cost of running donor upstream blocks alongside host blocks introduces runtime overhead that is not quantitatively profiled in terms of latency or FLOP trade-offs.
suggestions: Evaluate whether similar prefix-restoration dynamics hold when donor and host models do not share the exact same weight initialization.
Provide wall-clock inference latency and memory footprint comparisons between the stitched hybrid architecture and the intact donor model.

claims.text: Bansal and colleagues (NeurIPS 2021) study model stitching to evaluate representational compatibility between neural networks.
Geiger and colleagues (NeurIPS 2021) introduce interchange interventions to test causal properties of neural network representations.
Supplying the transplanted memory head with representations from its donor embeddings and first three blocks raised balanced accuracy to 90.32% compared to 10.43% for an untrained branch.
claims.source: Internal experimental benchmark results reported with paired 95% bootstrap intervals [79.04, 80.67]

novelty_vs_existing.title: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While Bansal et al. examined full-layer stitch layers between frozen vision/language networks, this work isolates single attention head transplantations conditioned on parallel native upstream prefix activations in transformers.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Causal Abstractions of Neural Networks
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies interchange intervention analysis to verify causal transmission through a hybridized donor-host transformer pathway rather than evaluating standalone NLI models.
